Get the NOAS04 Land Use Nomenclature

Source: R/noas.R
noas.Rd

Returns the hierarchical standard nomenclature NOAS04 of the Swiss land use statistics (Arealstatistik), separate from the measured values: 4 main domains, 17 base categories, 27 aggregated categories and 72 basic categories. Use it to label land use classes in four languages and to aggregate fine classes to coarser ones reproducibly.

Usage

noas(nClasses = 17, cache = TRUE, refresh = FALSE)

Arguments

nClasses

level(s) of the nomenclature, given by their number of classes: any of 4, 17, 27, 72.

cache

logical; if TRUE, results are read from and written to the local cache (see cacheList()).

refresh

logical; if TRUE, the source is queried again even if a cached copy exists.

Value

A data.frame with the columns level_n (number of classes of the level), noas_c (hierarchical code), noas_n (class number within the level, e.g. 1 to 17), parent_c (code of the parent class, NA for the main domains), noas_x_de, noas_x_fr, noas_x_it and noas_x_en.

Details

The nomenclature is read from the SDMX codelist CL_AREA_NOAS of the BFS dissemination service. If the service is unreachable and no cached copy exists, a German-only copy shipped with the package is used and a message says so.

Codes are hierarchical: the main domain is one digit, each finer level appends the two-digit class number of that level, e.g. "1" -> "102" (base category 2) -> "10202" (aggregated category 2) -> "1020203" (basic category 3).

See also

arealGemeinde() for the measured areas.

Other swiss.statistics: arealGemeinde(), popGemeinde()

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
noas(17)

# base category (17 classes) of each of the 72 basic categories
n72 <- noas(72)
n27 <- noas(27)
n72$noas17_c <- n27$parent_c[match(n72$parent_c, n27$noas_c)]
} # }
